title: Ombre buttercream, gradient layering on a cake
subtitle: How to blend a single colour from pale at the top to deep at the base
excerpt: An ombre buttercream cake is frosted in three or four shades of the same colour, darkening from top to base. The shades are applied in bands and then blended with a bench scraper to create a smooth gradient. The technique requires a turntable, a straight-sided cake, and patience at the blending stage.
sourceNotes: Ombre buttercream is a contemporary cake-decorating technique widely used in home and professional cake decoration.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Apply on the day of serving. The finished cake keeps covered in a cool room for 2 days.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thin base layer of buttercream applied to seal crumbs before the final decorative coating. It sets firm after a 30-minute chill and prevents crumbs from appearing in the finished finish.
A gradual blend from one shade to another, darker at one end and lighter at the other. In cake decorating, typically applied as bands of buttercream blended together on the sides of the cake.

content.text: buttercream finish blends colour bands on the outside of a chilled,

cake. Three or four shades blend together to produce a smooth gradient. The key steps are: keep the buttercream at the right temperature, apply the bands generously, and blend in a single clean pass with a scraper.

Make one large batch of vanilla buttercream. Divide into four equal portions. Leave one portion plain (the lightest shade). Add an increasing number of drops of gel food colouring to the other three, creating a pale, medium, and deep shade. Gel colouring is more concentrated and more stable than liquid colouring; it will not thin the buttercream.
Apply a thin crumb coat over the whole stacked cake, including the top. Chill for 30 minutes. The crumb coat must be firm before the ombre bands go on or the colours will drag and muddy.

Place the chilled cake on the turntable. Apply the darkest shade generously to the lower third of the cake with the icing spatula. Spread the medium shade on the middle third, and the pale shade on the upper third. Apply the lightest shade to the top.
Hold the bench scraper upright against the side of the cake, touching the turntable. Spin the turntable smoothly while holding the scraper still. This pulls the buttercream into a smooth band.
Wipe the scraper clean between passes. Repeat until the band boundaries blend into a soft gradient. Use the icing spatula to touch up any gaps before the final pass.

Buttercream at 18 to 22°C is pipeable and spreadable. Below 16°C it tears the crumb coat; above 24°C it slides off the cake. If the buttercream becomes too soft during application, chill the cake for 10 minutes and continue.
